text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MX-012","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D8","page":1,"quote":"80.5"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D11","page":1,"quote":"22"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D17","page":1,"quote":"22"}],"comment":"Dimensions D8, D11 and D17 define the length and width of keyways on a shaft, which are functional mating features for torque transmission, yet they carry no tolerance and fall back to the general machining tolerance. The designer should add specific tolerances (e.g., per a standard keyway fit) so the key seats properly with its mating key.","recommended_correction":"Add explicit tolerances to dimensions D8, D11 and D17 appropriate for keyway mating fits."},{"rule_id":"NM-002","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N4","page":1,"quote":"4) $FLASH HARD CHROME PLATING 15 TO 20 MICRONS,HARDNESS 850."},{"kind":"note","ref":"N5","page":1,"quote":"5) SURFACE FINISH:-Ra 0.2 TO 0.3 MICRONS."}],"comment":"Note N4 specifies flash hard chrome plating at 15–20 microns thickness, but note N5 requires a surface finish of Ra 0.2–0.3 microns; as-deposited hard chrome is far rougher than this and achieving that finish would require post-plating grinding that removes most or all of the specified plating thickness. This contradiction makes it impossible for manufacturing to satisfy both notes simultaneously. The designer should clarify whether the surface finish applies before or after plating, or adjust the plating thickness to allow for finishing stock.","recommended_correction":"Revise N4 or N5 to resolve the conflict between the plating thickness and the required final surface finish, specifying the sequence of operations if grinding after plating is intended."}]}
